statement: Ravi has $12$ identical stickers to put into $3$ different albums. Each album must get an even number of stickers, and an album may get no stickers at all. All $12$ stickers are used. In how many ways can he do this?

choices.misconception: I listed the different sets of amounts, like 6, 4, 2, but did not count which album gets which amount.
I made every album get at least 2 stickers, so I shared the 3 extra pairs among the albums and got C(5, 2) = 10.
I forgot the even rule and also made every album get at least one sticker, getting C(11, 2) = 55.
I forgot the even rule and counted every way to put 12 stickers into 3 albums, C(14, 2) = 91.

hints: Even amounts come in pairs. Think of the stickers as 6 pairs.
Now count the ways to put 6 identical pairs into 3 albums, where an album may get none.
Stars and bars: 6 stars and 2 bars, so C(8, 2).

solutions.reliable: Since every album gets an even number, glue the stickers into $6$ pairs, and each album gets a whole number of pairs, possibly $0$. The number of ways to put $6$ identical pairs into $3$ different albums is the number of ways to line up $6$ stars and $2$ bars, which is $\binom{8}{2} = 28$. As a check, if the first album gets $k$ pairs, the other two albums share $6 - k$ pairs in $7 - k$ ways, and $7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 28$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
